verify.name: content-parses
verify.expect: all SIX suites print OK, each naming how much it examined: posts PLUS rich-text fields restricting headings to h2-h6 + heading-level fixture runs + SCANNED post bodies + corpus headings (126 today); blockquote fixtures + corpus blockquotes; sanitize cases + corpus html nodes + embed blocks; smartypants cases + corpus text nodes + inline-code nodes; island-guard blog slug cases (incl. a cross-collection subset) + corpus slugs + PAGE slug cases (incl. a cross-collection subset) + corpus page slugs + control-character cases + .mdx documents inventoried + settings-path cases + island-name cases + icon-name cases; and page prose bodies + words + pages + blocks + empty rich-text fields skipped, all asserted to parse without an invalid_markdown node, PLUS rich-text fields restricting headings to h2-h6 + heading-level fixture runs + SCANNED bodies + corpus headings + pages asserted to render exactly one <h1> WITH A NON-EMPTY ACCESSIBLE NAME, with Vale's own file count reconciled against them. Treat the numbers as floors that grow when fixtures are added — but a suite that stops naming one of those categories has lost coverage, which is the failure this line exists to catch. Both heading scans report a count that is legitimately unfalsifiable on its own — 0 disallowed headings is what a working scan prints AND what a deleted one prints — which is why other numbers sit beside each: the fixture runs prove the h1 predicate can go red, and the scanned-body and page counts are reconciled against the bodies extracted and the pages parsed.
verify.why:
Aggregates check:content, check:blockquotes, check:sanitize, check:smartypants, check:island-guard and check:page-prose. Each asserts it ran over a non-empty corpus — a Tina collection, a Vale glob and an embed counter have all reported success over nothing on this branch. check:page-prose exists because a `.vale.ini` section pointed at content/pages/**/*.mdx reports '0 errors in 2 files' and KEEPS reporting it with banned words in the prose: the bodies live in YAML frontmatter, which Vale does not read. It extracts them, lints them as real files, and fails if Vale's trailing 'in N files' count does not equal the number it wrote — which is what catches the .vale.ini section being removed. It also asserts no block body authors an

, and that no page renders ZERO of them: src/lib/tina/pages.ts guarantees one

per page by reasoning about the BLOCK LIST, so a prose body — which is not a block — escapes it entirely, and both page documents were seeded by hand rather than through the admin whose schema now forbids it. The zero case is the same hand-edit path: seoTitle is `required: true`, which is FORM validation, and the generated GraphQL type is String!, which forbids null and permits the empty string — so a hand-written blank seoTitle on a page not led by a named Hero renders a document whose first heading is an h2. NON-EMPTY ACCESSIBLE NAME and not merely 'one

': `required: true` does not reject a field of spaces either, and until Task 3.3 the runtime tested `Boolean(name)` while this check tested `name.trim() !== ""` — so `name: " "` on a leading hero rendered `

` and the check reported the seoTitle the runtime never reached. Both now call `hasHeadingText` from src/lib/tina/heading-text.ts, a leaf module with no imports so the .mjs can load it under Node's type stripping. The schema half of the h1 rule is asserted over EVERY rich-text field — on every block template for pages, and recursively over the collection's fields and their templates for posts — not by field name, because checking one field by name would let a rich-text field added elsewhere ship with Heading 1 still on offer. check:content enforces the same rule for post bodies since Task 3.3, sharing the predicate, the allowed levels and the fixtures through scripts/lib/headings.mjs so the two cannot drift on what counts as an h1. The island-guard control-character cases exist to kill an `m` flag on the slug patterns: under /m the `$` anchors to a LINE end, so `about\n../settings/index` would validate while every other fixture still passed.

verify.name: tina-indexes-posts
verify.expect: OK: Tina indexes blog=17 settings=1 page=2
verify.why: `tinacms audit` prints '✅ Audit passed' and exits 0 on an EMPTY collection, so the counts must be asserted explicitly. A wrong collection path/format/glob would otherwise build all 59 pages with no posts, exit 0, and deploy. Asserts per-collection since Task 2.1: the script fails if a named collection is missing from the audit, if a count is wrong, AND if the audit reports a collection nobody asserted. That third mode did its job in Task 3.1 — the `page` collection failed this gate with 'audit reported the page collection but no expected count was given' until `page=2` was added here. `page=2` is home.mdx + about.mdx; a page added in the CMS must be added to this count, and until Task 3.2 lands the catch-all route that is the ONLY gate that notices a page document at all.

verify.name: build-and-routes
verify.command: bun run build:local && find dist/client -name '*.html' | sed 's|^dist/client||' | sort | diff .baseline/routes.txt -
verify.expect: only difference is an added /admin/index.html (the TinaCMS admin SPA); all 59 site routes present
verify.why: USE `build:local` UNTIL PHASE 4 LANDS. Three build scripts, and the difference is which client gets generated, not just where content comes from — per `tinacms build --help`: `build` (--content=local) reads content off the filesystem but generates a PRODUCTION client pointing at TinaCloud, and the CLI refuses without clientId+token ('--content=local requires ... since the generated client must point to TinaCloud', @tinacms/cli/dist/index.js:3526) — so it cannot run before Phase 4; `build:cloud` (no flags) also fetches content from TinaCloud; `build:local` (--local --skip-cloud-checks) runs everything locally, needs no credentials, and is the only one that works today. The trade is that --local bakes url:'http://localhost:4001/graphql' into the client, which is harmless for all 59 prerendered pages (those queries ran at build time) but leaves the one on-demand route, /tina-island/[name], pointing at localhost on the Worker. Output moved to dist/client + dist/server when the Cloudflare adapter landed, so the route diff must target dist/client. Tina's datalayer defaults to 9000, held by another tool on this machine; all three scripts pin --datalayer-port 9007. All three set NODE_ENV=production, because `tinacms build` otherwise runs its subcommand with NODE_ENV=development, which folds import.meta.env.DEV to true and compiles postFilter to `return true` — publishing every draft and scheduled post. At Phase 4, switch this gate and .github/workflows/daily-deploy.yml to `build`.

verify.name: lint
verify.expect: EXACTLY 3 errors + 1 warning: 'Found 3 errors.' / 'Found 1 warning.' over 108 files (93 when this line was written at Task 2.1; the repo has grown, so read the ERROR COUNT, not the file count). Four diagnostics over three files: the 3 errors are DESIGN.json (format), src/utils/og-templates/post.js (format), src/utils/og-templates/site.js (format); the 1 warning is src/utils/og-templates/post.js:2:8 lint/correctness/noUnusedImports (unused `SITE` import) — so post.js accounts for two of the four, and four diagnostics is NOT four errors. All pre-existing on main. src/components/Header.astro was on this list until Task 2.1, when the settings-prop edit supplied the blank line after its imports that was its only complaint — its absence is a fix, not a regression.
verify.why: Not a clean gate. Any file outside that list is a regression introduced by this branch. READ THE COUNT, AND READ EVERY '━━━' HEADER — DO NOT grep the output for a file-name pattern. Biome prints format diagnostics as 'path format' but lint/assist diagnostics as 'path:line:col rule', so a filter anchored on the filename followed by a space silently hides every assist/organizeImports failure. That is exactly how Task 2.1 reported '3 files, clean' while the gate was actually failing on 4 branch-modified files (src/constants.ts, src/layouts/AboutLayout.astro, src/pages/blog/[...page].astro, src/pages/tags/[tag]/[...page].astro). The 'Found N errors' line never reconciled with the filtered list and that was the tell.

verify.name: dev-smoke
verify.expect: OK naming 7 dev URL(s) over PLAIN HTTP on localhost:4321: / /about /blog/git-and-diffs /admin/index.html /admin(302) /_image(500, bare) and a real /_image derivative taken from the homepage's own srcset — plus an 'ok N admin script URL(s) are http://' line. Treat 7 as a floor that grows when URLs are added; a run naming FEWER has lost coverage. The count is asserted non-zero in the script, because a fetch loop over an empty list reports zero failures, which is what success looks like.
verify.why: The only gate that runs the site rather than building it, and it exists because every other gate is build-time. `imageService: "compile"` wires /_image to @astrojs/cloudflare/image-transform-endpoint, whose first line imports `cloudflare:workers` — a module that exists only in workerd. `astro dev` runs in Node, so every page with an <Image> died with FailedToLoadModuleSSR, and it survived eleven tasks and six reviewers because no build ever runs with `command === "dev"`. Status alone is NOT the assertion: Vite answers 200 and injects an error overlay into the body, so the body is checked for FailedToLoadModuleSSR / cloudflare:workers / Could not import / the overlay elements. MUTATION-PROVED: removing the `image.endpoint` dev override turns BOTH /_image entries red (bare one on the body marker, real one on status/content-type) while the five page URLs still pass — which is why the two /_image entries are not redundant. The bare /_image expects 500 BY DESIGN: no href means parseURL returns undefined and the endpoint throws into its own catch, so healthy and broken differ in the BODY, not the status. WHAT IT CANNOT PROVE: it is not a browser. It fetches documents and does not execute them or load sub-resources, so it would have passed while /admin was completely unusable — an https admin page cannot load TinaCMS's http :4001 scripts, and the browser blocked every one while the document still returned 200. The admin script-scheme assertion is the narrow machine-checkable part of that; clicking through /admin stays a human job. Shuts the server down in a `finally` and on SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit, because `astro dev` daemonises and a stranded daemon holds 4321 while the NEXT run silently attaches to it.
